questions.question: In covering a distance of 162 km, Anmol takes 3 hours more than Nikhil. If Anmol doubles his speed, then he would take 6 hours less than Nikhil. Anmol's speed is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional.

As Anmol doubles his speed, his time gets halved. Reduction in time = T − T/2 = T/2.

Total time saved = 3 hours (initially more than Nikhil) + 6 hours (later less than Nikhil) = 9 hours.

⇒ T/2 = 9 hours ⇒ Original Time (T) = 18 hours.

Anmol's speed = Distance ÷ Time = 162 ÷ 18 = 9 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 162 km

Anmol takes 3 hours more than Nikhil initially.

If Anmol doubles his speed, he takes 6 hours less than Nikhil.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ (17⁰.²⁴)z = (17⁰.⁵¹)⁴

Power of a Power Rule

Product Rule of Exponents

When multiplying two or more terms that have the same base, simply add their exponents together: am × aⁿ = am ⁺ ⁿ

Quotient Rule of Exponents

When dividing two terms with the identical base, subtract the denominator's exponent from the numerator's exponent: am ÷ aⁿ = am − ⁿ

questions.question: If X = (sin²theta)/(1+costheta) - (sintheta)/(cottheta - {cosec)theta} , then the value of (X-1) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Substitute θ = 45° into the given expression.

X = (1/2) ÷ (1 + 1/√2) − (1/√2) ÷ (1 − √2)

X = 1 / (2 + √2) + 1 / (2 − √2) = [(2 − √2) + (2 + √2)] ÷ (4 − 2) = 4 ÷ 2 = 2

Required value = X − 1 = 2 − 1 = 1.

From the options, sec²(45°) − tan²(45°) = (√2)² − (1)² = 2 − 1 = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is sec²θ − tan²θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

X = sin²θ / (1 + cosθ) − sinθ / (cotθ − cosecθ)

**Formula Used:**

sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ = (1 − cosθ)(1 + cosθ)

cotθ = cosθ / sinθ | cosecθ = 1 / sinθ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Term 1 = sin²θ / (1 + cosθ) = (1 − cos²θ) / (1 + cosθ)

⇒ Term 1 = (1 − cosθ)(1 + cosθ) / (1 + cosθ) = 1 − cosθ

⇒ Term 2 = sinθ / (cotθ − cosecθ) = sinθ / [(cosθ − 1) / sinθ]

⇒ Term 2 = sin²θ / (cosθ − 1) = (1 − cos²θ) / (cosθ − 1)

⇒ Term 2 = −(cos²θ − 1) / (cosθ − 1)

⇒ Term 2 = −(cosθ − 1)(cosθ + 1) / (cosθ − 1) = −(1 + cosθ)

⇒ X = Term 1 − Term 2 = (1 − cosθ) − [−(1 + cosθ)]

⇒ X = 1 − cosθ + 1 + cosθ = 2

⇒ The required value is (X − 1) = 2 − 1 = 1

⇒ Checking the options, the standard identity sec²θ − tan²θ equals 1.

**∴ The correct answer is sec²θ − tan²θ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental trigonometric identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Value Substitution Method

When simplifying complex expressions, substituting standard angles (30°, 45°, 60°) quickly identifies the correct option. Always avoid angles that make any denominator zero.

Reciprocal Trigonometric Ratios

Key relationships to remember: cosecθ = 1 / sinθ, secθ = 1 / cosθ, and cotθ = 1 / tanθ = cosθ / sinθ.
</p

questions.question: The value of (3⁰ + 3−² + 3−¹ ) × 27 is _______.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expand the bracket and multiply 27 directly to each term to avoid fraction addition:

⇒ (1 + 1/9 + 1/3) × 27

⇒ (1 × 27) + (1/9 × 27) + (1/3 × 27)

⇒ 27 + 3 + 9 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (3⁰ + 3−² + 3−¹) × 27

**Formula Used:**

a⁰ = 1

a−ⁿ = 1 / aⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Substitute the values of powers using exponent rules:

⇒ 3⁰ = 1

⇒ 3−² = 1 / 3² = 1/9

⇒ 3−¹ = 1 / 3¹ = 1/3

⇒ Add the values inside the bracket by taking the LCM of the denominators (9, 3, and 1), which is 9:

⇒ (1 + 1/9 + 1/3) = (9 + 1 + 3) / 9 = 13/9

⇒ Now multiply the sum by 27:

⇒ (13 / 9) × 27

⇒ 13 × (27 ÷ 9)

⇒ 13 × 3 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Zero Exponent Rule

Any non-zero real number raised to the power of zero is always equal to 1: a⁰ = 1.

Negative Exponent Rule

A negative exponent implies the reciprocal of the base raised to the corresponding positive power: a−ⁿ = 1 / aⁿ.

BODMAS Rule

Expressions must be evaluated following the order of Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Product Rule of Exponents

When multiplying terms with the same base, add the exponents: am × aⁿ = am⁺ⁿ.
</p

questions.question: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 19% and its height is increased by 102%, then what is the percentage increase (closest integer) in its volume?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a cylinder is directly proportional to r² × h.

Multiplying factor for radius = 1 − 0.19 = 0.81

Multiplying factor for height = 1 + 1.02 = 2.02

New Volume = (0.81)² × 2.02 × Old Volume = 0.6561 × 2.02 × Old Volume = 1.325322 × Old Volume

Percentage increase = (1.325322 − 1) × 100 = 32.53% ≈ 33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Decrease in radius = 19%

Increase in height = 102%

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder (V) = πr²h

 
 Initial Volume = 100%
 
 New Volume ≈ 133%
 
• 
 
• 
 

 + 33%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let original radius = r and original height = h

⇒ Original Volume (V₁) = πr²h

⇒ New radius (r₂) = r − 0.19r = 0.81r

⇒ New height (h₂) = h + 1.02h = 2.02h

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = π × (0.81r)² × (2.02h)

⇒ V₂ = π × 0.6561r² × 2.02h

⇒ V₂ = 1.325322 πr²h

⇒ Increase in Volume = V₂ − V₁

⇒ Increase in Volume = 1.325322 πr²h − πr²h = 0.325322 πr²h

⇒ Percentage Increase = (0.325322 πr²h ÷ πr²h) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase = 32.5322% ≈ 33%

**∴ The correct answer is 33%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

The fundamental formula to calculate the percentage change is: [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Successive Percentage Change

When multiple successive percentage changes occur, applying a net multiplying factor corresponding to the direct proportionality (like r²h for volume) offers the fastest calculation method instead of calculating step-by-step.

Volume of Cylinder & Cone

Volume of a Right Circular Cylinder = πr²h. Volume of a Right Circular Cone = (1/3)πr²h. In both formulas, the volume varies directly with the square of the radius and linearly with the height.
</p

questions.question: A sum of money triples itself at a certain rate of compound interest in 12 years. In how many years will it amount to 27 times of itself?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes n times in T years at compound interest, it becomes nm times in m × T years.

Here, the sum becomes 3 times in 12 years.

We need it to become 27 times, which is 3³ times (meaning m = 3).

Therefore, required time = 3 × 12 = 36 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 36 years.**

**Calculations:**

⇒ 3P = P(1 + R ÷ 100)¹²

⇒ 3 = (1 + R ÷ 100)¹² ... (Equation 1)

Let the required time taken for the sum to become 27 times be T years.

⇒ 27P = P(1 + R ÷ 100)T

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant over the years. In Compound Interest, the interest of the previous period is added to the principal to compute the interest for the next period, generating interest on interest.

Rule of 72

A quick mathematical formula to estimate the number of years required to double an invested sum at a given annual compound interest rate (R): Years ≈ 72 ÷ R.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When compound interest is calculated half-yearly, the annual rate of interest is halved (R ÷ 2) and the time period is doubled (2T) in the fundamental calculation formula.

questions.question: By selling an article at (4)/(13) of its actual selling price, Hitesh incurs a loss of 22%. If he sells it at 60% of its actual selling price, then the profit percentage is:

⇒ SP₂ = 60% of Actual SP = 0.60 × 13 units = 7.8 units

⇒ SP₂ in terms of CP = 7.8 × 19.5% = 152.1% of CP

⇒ Profit % = 152.1% − 100% = 52.1%

Selling at 4/13 of actual SP results in a 22% loss.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the effective discount percentage is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

If a dealer claims to sell at cost price but uses a false weight, Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.

questions.question: Let A and B be two regular polygons. The sum of the interior angles of A is 1260°. Each interior angle of B exceeds its exterior angle by 90°. Find the sum of the number of sides of A and B.

Interior and Exterior Angles

questions.question: Pipe P can fill 2/9 part of a tank in 20 hours, and pipe Q can fill 2/5 part of the same tank in 18 hours. Both P and Q were kept open for 3 hours, then both were closed. Pipe R alone was then opened and it emptied the water in the tank in 4 hours. Pipes P, Q and R together can fill the empty tank in:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time for P to fill tank = 20 × (9/2) = 90 hours; Time for Q = 18 × (5/2) = 45 hours.

Let Total Work = 360 units. Efficiency: P = 4 units/hr, Q = 8 units/hr.

Work done by P and Q in 3 hours = (4 + 8) × 3 = 36 units.

R empties 36 units in 4 hours ⇒ R's efficiency = −36 ÷ 4 = −9 units/hr.

Time taken by P, Q, and R together = 360 ÷ (4 + 8 − 9) = 360 ÷ 3 = 120 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 hours.**

Total capacity is assumed as the LCM of time taken by individual pipes. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time.

Negative Work

A pipe that empties a tank performs negative work. Its efficiency is subtracted from the efficiency of the filling pipes.

Combined Work Rule

If multiple pipes operate simultaneously, their combined efficiency is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.
